profile.label: Authored step-free demo
profile.description: A synthetic repair-planning profile with explicit edge assessments, equal-weight destinations and hypothetical blocker removal. It does not establish legal compliance or safe real-world navigation.

assumptions: This is an entirely synthetic schematic near coordinate [0, 0]. Nodes, topology, evidence, edge lengths and condition assessments are authored illustrations, not field geography, measurements or observations.

Every destination has weight one and uses the fixed arrival origin and step-free demo profile. Edge direction is explicit, visual intersections create no connections, and the archive has no connecting edge.
Every edge has an explicit authored assessment. Passability is independent of evidence review status; rejected, accepted and pending reviews do not override named blockers or unknown coverage.

Costs are illustrative assumed amounts in USD cents, not supplier quotes: repair A costs 200 cents, repair B costs 200 cents and repair C costs 400 cents. The studio repair cost is unknown and is excluded rather than treated as free. The default shared budget is 400 cents.

Severity is an authored integer scale from 1 (least severe) to 5 (most severe), independent of trip benefit: C is 5, the studio obstruction is 4, A is 3 and B is 2. These are illustrative condition ratings, not measured inspection results.

The library and student center share two sequential blocked links. A and B each restore zero destinations alone; together they restore both named destinations. C is a separate worse-condition repair that restores only the hall. The cafe is already reachable and is never counted as newly restored.

The studio walk has unknown coverage without a named blocker; its shorter parallel shortcut has both unknown coverage and a known crate blocker. Clearing the shortcut crate would still leave its coverage unknown, never passable.

Each repair clears one named blocker in an immutable hypothetical projection. It does not change evidence, review records, source assessments or unknown coverage. Exactness applies only to the supplied bounded candidates and assumptions, not real-world outcomes.
